discoveries.choice: The file holds a single terse, unpunctuated line of plain lowercase prose rather than any structured or formatted content.
discoveries.whyItMatters: For a phase whose goal is to establish the notes artifact, the entire observable behavior of the deliverable is its shape and content: one short, human-readable line with no headings, bullet markers, key/value metadata, or terminating period. Anything downstream that parses, summarizes, or versions notes.txt can rely on there being exactly one line and no markup, so this minimalism is the contract's real content rather than an incidental detail.

alternatives.option: Emit structured or formatted notes (markdown headings, bullets, timestamps, or key/value pairs).
alternatives.consequence: Would give downstream consumers more to parse and richer semantics, but would contradict the observed artifact and add format commitments the phase never agreed to.

alternatives.option: Emit multiple lines or a longer narrative body.
alternatives.consequence: Would carry more information, but breaks the single-line shape that is the only verifiable property here and invites per-line expectations the file does not satisfy.

alternatives.option: Emit no content or an empty placeholder file.
alternatives.consequence: Would preserve minimalism to the point of having nothing to review; the phase would have no observable deliverable and no basis for acceptance.

recommendation.choice: Keep the single terse, unpunctuated lowercase line.
recommendation.reason: It matches the observed artifact exactly, gives downstream readers a stable and trivially parseable shape, and avoids inventing format or content guarantees that were never requested.
